author: naughtypip
text: Josh wrote: Yup. That's a 3drive. I really don't know where the term comes from, but the CP in it and the psychology behind it make alot of sense. It's quite a common pattern, and provides very low risk setups. The CP is a by product of what is happening beneath the pattern, I won't say anymore as it's best for people to figure things out for themselves, I just know it as something different to do with market phases. I definitely agree with the statement in bold - too many people don't know how to think for themselves, the only way you become a great trader is by discovering things for yourself. I know I ask people to look for patterns - this is to get a concrete starting point in learning to read price. Once folk start to seek out these patterns, they'll begin to notice a myriad other phenomena, which will become very important EUREKA moments for them - I just love those EUREKA moments:cheer: When you talk about the cp being a bi product of what is happening beneath the pattern, are you hinting of accumulation and distribution?

author: Nosbigs
text:
The 3Drive onto S/D can be a strong indication that price will turn.

It shows that price advances are slowing down, while compressing up/down, taking out orders as it goes.

pair, any timeframe

author: Simon
text:
There's an irony to this one. I spent so much of yesterday determined to see compression in the market that in the end I overlooked what the market was actually telling me, which is that it was 3Driving down to the gift area that was a W1 SR Flip confluenced with M30 Demand.

This shouldn't happen again. It seems one of the very positive benefits of doing one's homework in the live market is that it tends to stick.

A Beatles lyric springs to mind. I won't bore you with the entire song but it has something to do with "getting better all the time"!
